meta.name: Qualify and route dental leads with GPT-4, GoHighLevel, Twilio, and Meta Ads

name: Local Service Lead Qualification & Follow-Up Engine

nodes.name: Set Workflow Defaults
nodes.notes: Centralised config: GHL/Twilio/Slack/Calendar/Pinecone credentials and IDs, plus scoring/timing thresholds referenced throughout the workflow. Replace every YOUR_* placeholder before activating.

nodes.name: Prepare Lead Data
nodes.notes: Normalizes the 3 merged intake shapes (website form webhook, Twilio SMS reply, Meta Lead Ads) into one common lead record. Converted from Set to Code since normalization needs per-source branching logic, not a flat field mapping.

nodes.name: Lead Qualifier Agent
nodes.notes: Classifies each inbound lead into a treatment category (feeding Route by Lead Treatment), scores it via the Calculate Lead Score tool, and checks GHL history/calendar availability/knowledge base as needed.

options.systemMessage:
You are a lead qualification assistant for a local dental/aesthetic practice. Your job is to read an inbound lead's details and:

1. Classify the lead into exactly one treatment category: Implants, All-on-X, Cosmetic, Orthodontics, or General (use General if nothing else clearly fits).
2. Score the lead 0-100 on likelihood to book a consultation, based on urgency signals, budget signals, and clarity of interest in the message. Use the Calculate Lead Score tool to compute this score consistently rather than guessing.
3. Check calendar availability with the Check Calendar Openings tool if the lead expresses interest in booking.
4. Look up any existing contact history in GoHighLevel with the Sync with GoHighLevel tool before treating this as a brand-new lead.
5. Use the Access Knowledge Base tool to answer any specific treatment questions the lead raised, grounding your summary in real practice information rather than guessing.

Always return your final answer in the structured format required. Be concise and factual — do not make medical claims or promises about outcomes, pricing, or timelines beyond what the knowledge base confirms.

nodes.name: Capture Conversation Memory
nodes.notes: Keeps conversation context isolated per lead (keyed by phone/contact ID) rather than sharing memory across unrelated leads.

nodes.name: Access Knowledge Base
nodes.notes: Retrieval tool over the practice's Pinecone knowledge base — index name pulled from Set Workflow Defaults. Populate the index with real treatment/FAQ/pricing content before relying on this.

parameters.toolDescription: Searches the practice's treatment information knowledge base (procedures, pricing ranges, financing options, FAQs) to answer specific questions a lead raised.

nodes.name: Check Calendar Openings
nodes.notes: Calls a separate sub-workflow (not included here) that queries Google Calendar for open slots — replace YOUR_CALENDAR_CHECK_SUBWORKFLOW_ID with a real n8n workflow ID that performs the calendar lookup and returns available slots.

parameters.description: Checks the practice's Google Calendar for open consultation slots in the next 7 days. Call this when a lead expresses interest in booking.

nodes.name: Sync with GoHighLevel
nodes.notes: Calls a separate sub-workflow (not included here) that looks up or creates the GHL contact by phone/email — replace YOUR_GHL_SYNC_SUBWORKFLOW_ID with a real n8n workflow ID.

parameters.description: Looks up this lead's existing contact record and pipeline history in GoHighLevel by phone/email, or creates a new contact if none exists. Call this before treating a lead as brand-new.

nodes.name: Calculate Lead Score
nodes.notes: Deterministic scoring tool (not left to LLM guesswork): urgency/budget keywords, treatment value, message detail, and contact completeness.

parameters.description: Computes a deterministic 0-100 lead score from urgency, budget, and message-clarity signals. Call this instead of guessing a score.

nodes.name: Route by Lead Treatment
nodes.notes: FIX: All 6 conditions were '' equals '' (always matched the first branch — Implants — regardless of the AI's actual classification), and only 1 of 6 outputs was wired downstream (the other 5 dead-ended). Now routes on the AI agent's real treatment_category output, with a fallback output for anything unmatched, and all 6 outputs (5 named + 1 fallback) are wired to Fetch GHL Contact Info.

nodes.name: Fetch GHL Contact Info
nodes.notes: Looks up the GHL contact by phone number to attach pipeline/custom-field data to this lead.

nodes.name: Fetch GHL Pipeline Stage
nodes.notes: Fetches this contact's current pipeline/opportunity stage, if one already exists (returning lead vs. brand-new).

nodes.name: Fetch GHL Custom Field Data
nodes.notes: Fetches the full contact record including custom fields (treatment history, referral source, etc.) before branching into priority checking, messaging, scheduling, and logging.

parameters.url: ={{ $('Set Workflow Defaults').first().json.GHL_API_BASE }}/contacts/{{ $('Fetch GHL Contact Info').first().json.contact?.id || $('Fetch GHL Contact Info').first().json.id }}

nodes.name: Send SMS via Twilio
nodes.notes: Sends an immediate acknowledgement SMS to every new lead regardless of priority — Twilio credentials need to be attached separately in n8n's credential UI (Twilio isn't a header-auth service like GHL).

parameters.message: =Hi {{ $('Prepare Lead Data').first().json.lead_name }}, thanks for reaching out to {{ $('Prepare Lead Data').first().json.practice_name }}! We received your enquiry about {{ $('Lead Qualifier Agent').first().json.output?.treatment_category || 'our services' }} and a team member will be in touch shortly. Reply STOP to opt out.

nodes.name: Send Email via SMTP
nodes.notes: Sends an intake confirmation email — skipped naturally if the lead has no email (SMTP will fail gracefully or should be gated on lead_email being non-empty if strict validation is desired).

parameters.subject: =Thanks for reaching out to {{ $('Prepare Lead Data').first().json.practice_name }}

nodes.name: Check Lead Priority
nodes.notes: FIX: Had zero conditions (an empty AND with nothing to compare, so behavior was undefined). Now compares the AI agent's lead_score against HIGH_PRIORITY_SCORE_THRESHOLD from config — TRUE (high priority) triggers an immediate AI voice call and Slack alert.

nodes.name: Initiate AI Voice Call
nodes.notes: Fires only for high-priority leads (Check Lead Priority TRUE branch). Uses a static TwiML script — replace with a real AI voice agent integration (e.g. an ElevenLabs/Vapi call) if a genuinely conversational call is required rather than a one-way announcement.

nodes.name: Post Alert to Slack
nodes.notes: Alerts the team's hot-lead Slack channel whenever Check Lead Priority is TRUE.

parameters.text: =🔥 High-priority lead: {{ $('Prepare Lead Data').first().json.lead_name }} ({{ $('Prepare Lead Data').first().json.lead_phone }}) — {{ $('Lead Qualifier Agent').first().json.output?.treatment_category }}, score {{ $('Lead Qualifier Agent').first().json.output?.lead_score }}/100. {{ $('Lead Qualifier Agent').first().json.output?.summary }}

nodes.name: Schedule Meeting in Calendar
nodes.notes: Provisionally books a next-day consultation slot as a placeholder hold — adjust start/end to use real availability from the Check Calendar Openings tool's result rather than a fixed next-day offset once that sub-workflow is wired up.

additionalFields.description: =Lead source: {{ $('Prepare Lead Data').first().json.source }}. Score: {{ $('Lead Qualifier Agent').first().json.output?.lead_score }}. Summary: {{ $('Lead Qualifier Agent').first().json.output?.summary }}

nodes.name: Log to Database
nodes.notes: Logs every qualified lead to a Postgres 'leads' table — replace 'leads' with your real table name if different, and ensure the table's columns match the auto-mapped fields (lead_name, lead_phone, lead_email, treatment_interest, source, etc.).

nodes.name: When SMS Reply Received
nodes.notes: FIX: Had empty parameters and no credentials — a Twilio trigger with no config would never register a real webhook. Now configured to fire on incoming SMS messages.

nodes.name: When Meta Lead Ad Received
nodes.notes: FIX: page/form resource-locator values were empty strings — replaced with placeholders to be swapped for real IDs.

nodes.name: Reply to Facebook DMs
nodes.notes: Only meaningful for meta_lead_ad-sourced leads (no Facebook messenger thread exists for website/SMS leads) — this fires for every lead regardless of source since Fetch GHL Custom Field Data fans out unconditionally; consider gating this on source === 'meta_lead_ad' if noisy Graph API calls for non-Facebook leads become an issue.

nodes.name: When Follow-Up Time Reached
nodes.notes: FIX: Was an empty interval (undefined behavior). Now checks for unresponsive leads every 6 hours.

nodes.name: Fetch Unresponsive GHL Leads
nodes.notes: Pulls contacts tagged as unresponsive (adjust the tag name/filter to match your real GHL tagging convention) that are due for a follow-up touch (older than FOLLOW_UP_DAYS_UNRESPONSIVE).

nodes.name: Follow-Up Agent
nodes.notes: Decides the right re-engagement approach per unresponsive lead. Its output feeds Route by Follow-Up Type.

options.systemMessage:
You are a follow-up strategist for a local dental/aesthetic practice. For each unresponsive lead, decide exactly one follow-up type:

- Re-engage: the lead showed real interest but went quiet — worth a direct, personalized SMS/call attempt
- Nurture: the lead is early-stage or low-urgency — worth a gentle informational email instead of a hard sell
- Voice Call: the lead is high-value or previously expressed urgency — worth a live callback attempt
- Default: use this only if none of the above clearly fits

Base your decision on how much time has passed, the treatment interest, and any conversation history in memory. Do not fabricate details not present in the record.

nodes.name: OpenAI GPT-4 Follow-Up
nodes.notes: Language model backing the Follow-Up Agent.

nodes.name: Route by Follow-Up Type
nodes.notes: FIX: Previously had broken always-true empty-string conditions AND zero outgoing connections (entire follow-up branch was dead code). Now routes on Follow-Up Agent's structured follow_up_type output, with a fallback (Default) branch for anything unmatched.

nodes.name: Fetch Performance Metrics
nodes.notes: Pulls the last 7 days of lead records from the leads table (populated by Log to Database) for weekly reporting.

nodes.name: Aggregate Metrics for Dashboard
nodes.notes: FIX: Was an empty Set node with no aggregation logic. Converted to a Code node that computes real totals, high-priority counts, category breakdown, and average score from the fetched rows.

nodes.name: Build Dashboard Report
nodes.notes: FIX: Was an empty Set node. Now formats the aggregated metrics into a real report title/body for posting to GHL and emailing to the team.

assignments.name: reportBody

nodes.name: Post Report to GHL Dashboard
nodes.notes: FIX: Was an empty HTTP node. Posts the weekly report summary as a GHL note (adjust the endpoint to a real dashboard/reporting resource if your GHL setup has one).

nodes.notes: FIX: Was an empty Email node (existing SMTP credentials preserved, not overwritten).

parameters.content:
## Local Service Lead Qualification & Follow-Up Engine

### How it works

New leads arrive through a website form webhook, an inbound SMS reply, or a Meta Lead Ad, and are merged into a single stream and normalized into a common record alongside workflow-wide configuration such as GoHighLevel credentials and score thresholds. An AI Lead Qualifier Agent scores and categorizes each lead using a knowledge base, calendar availability, a GHL sync tool, and a deterministic scoring function, then the lead is routed by treatment category and enriched with contact, pipeline, and custom field data from GoHighLevel. A priority check decides whether the lead gets an immediate high-touch response (SMS, voice call, calendar booking, Slack alert to the team) or a standard acknowledgement (email, database log, Facebook reply). On a recurring schedule, unresponsive leads are re-fetched from GHL and handed to a Follow-Up Agent that decides whether to re-engage, nurture, or attempt a voice callback, routing to the same outreach actions. A separate weekly schedule aggregates recent lead activity into a performance report delivered to GHL and the team's inbox.

### Setup steps

- Configure Set Workflow Defaults with your real practice name, GoHighLevel API base/token/location ID, Twilio number, Slack channel, Google Calendar ID, Pinecone index name, dashboard email, and scoring thresholds.
- Add real credentials for OpenAI, Twilio, Slack, Google Calendar, Postgres, Facebook Lead Ads / Graph API, and Pinecone wherever a YOUR_*_CREDENTIAL_ID placeholder appears.
- Replace the placeholder sub-workflow IDs on the Check Calendar Openings and Sync with GoHighLevel tool nodes with real sub-workflow IDs once those are built.
- Set real page/form values on When Meta Lead Ad Received and confirm the Postgres leads table schema matches the fields written by Log to Database and read by Fetch Performance Metrics.
- Review the system prompts on Lead Qualifier Agent and Follow-Up Agent, and adjust the message templates on the SMS/email/Slack/voice-call action nodes to match your practice's tone.

### Customization

Adjust lead scoring weights in Calculate Lead Score's code, change the routing categories in Route by Lead Treatment or Route by Follow-Up Type to match your service offerings, and edit Aggregate Metrics for Dashboard if you want different metrics in the weekly report.

## Capture leads from all channels

Leads arrive from a website form webhook, an inbound SMS reply, or a Meta Lead Ad, are merged into one stream, and normalized into a common lead record alongside workflow-wide configuration.

## AI lead qualification

An AI agent scores and categorizes each lead using a knowledge base, calendar and GHL tools, and a scoring function, with per-lead memory and a structured output parser.

## Route by treatment and enrich from GHL

Leads are routed by treatment category, then enriched with contact, pipeline, and custom field data pulled from GoHighLevel, before a priority check decides urgency.

## Deliver outreach and follow-up actions

Depending on lead priority and follow-up routing, this cluster sends the SMS, email, Facebook reply, voice call, Slack alert, calendar booking, or database log that closes the loop with the lead.

## Re-engage unresponsive leads

On a recurring schedule, unresponsive GHL leads are fetched and handed to a follow-up AI agent that decides whether to re-engage, nurture, or attempt a voice call.

## Weekly performance reporting

On a weekly schedule, recent lead records are fetched from the database, aggregated into summary metrics, and delivered as a report to GHL and the team's inbox.
